name: CHERT
one_line: Chamfer-blade box: tapered camo blades cut the two aft corners and carry the door zip in their seam, so panel line = camo break = door; solid two-tone body, roll-top, CORRIE B.2 wings/pouch/pockets
corrie_b2_bag_system_basis: corrie.build() body group 533.1 + IMP-1/2/4/6/8 + fly F-01 x G-2 shell ratio (form.corrie_parts_g)
volume_basis: cloth-sim fill case, closed to the fill line, mean of 15/19/23 in (pouch, wings, pockets not counted); design-rule volume 76.94 L

cg_notes.limits: HA-LS-1 rev C: fill <= 205, meat <= 190 (y, mm, mass-weighted with 1 kg pouch + 85 mm spotter); rounding > 0 reads up to +4 mm (corrie_body.md 11.4)

features: Chamfer blades: the two aft vertical corners cut by a camo facet tapering 60 x 55 mm (floor) to 32 x 26 mm (collar seam); one camo U piece (blades + kick strip), creased not seamed
Door zip in the blade | aft-face seam (#10 coil, 2 sliders, 1.23 m): the camo break, the panel line and the door are one line; door = the whole aft face z 110-650
Fang insets (camo) low on each gusset, one straight seam, joining the blades into a wrap-round lower corner
Two-tone solid blocking: olive faces, dark collar + hinge band + roll, camo only on the outline (disruptive edge placement, docs/research/bag_comp_form.md)
Hexagon boxed floor carries the chamfer into the base
IMP-6R right-strap snack / GPS stretch pocket (fixes the snack miss on S-L belts)
CORRIE B.2 kept: roll-top, 2.7 L pouch, wings with tripod right and scope sleeve left, hipbelt pockets, holster, hydration sleeve, door pocket, frame interface, rain fly
Uniform-fill CG 0.7 mm forward of CORRIE at a taller body (chamfers remove aft-corner volume)
risks: 15 in meat CG 187.4 mm (limit 190, margin 2.6; reported at 1 mm contact rounding, so <= ~188 raw): tighter than CORRIE's 184.4 because the body is 36 mm taller to hold 85 L after the chamfers; prototype plumb CG check at 15 in with 30 kg on IM1-IM3 is mandatory
Door is narrower at the bottom: 163 mm at z 110 vs CORRIE 198 mm (wider at the top: 320 vs 304 mm)
The #10 door zip sits on a fold (blade | door seam at the chamfer crease): untested; it needs the loaded zip test and a sewing jig/notches so a beginner sets the zip straight before the facet folds

Camo blade U and fangs in 630D printable (290 g/m2) are stiffer and heavier than 330D; the sim models them as 330D (ASSUMPTION). The U-shaped cut wastes its centre on the marker unless the fangs and tabs nest there

Mass +17.6 g vs CORRIE B.2: shell +4.8 g (taller body, 630D camo blade U + fangs replacing the kick appliques), collar -3.2, door zip -0.5, fly -0.4, and the 17 g IMP-6R snack pocket (ASSUMPTION mass)

Access at belt M: sheep 8-day still misses bottle #2 (hourly) and beanie/gloves + poles at glassing (they end up above the z 650 door hinge in the taller body); day hunt kill kit is the CORRIE packing-order artifact
Fill line 41.6 in above the floor (CORRIE 40.2): roll-top 36 mm higher, check prone/head-tilt clearance
Wings, pouch, roll, tripod and pockets are placed render geometry on the simulated body (as CORRIE); the float-mode render bakes the 170 mm shift because the Cycles port does not apply it
Name CHERT and the chamfer-zip construction got a short search only, not a trademark or FTO clearance
